summary: conv-context-next preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (v1.3.13), extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the package-local math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob (string-array rotation via `WV8StW`, decoder `hc1jfK9`, `_0xXXXX` identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with no documented relationship to the package's advertised purpose of a small conversation-context helper. Using a foreign runtime fetched at install time to execute an opaque sibling payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: install-time execution of attacker-controlled code that bypasses Node-based observability and sandboxing. The package name also closely mirrors an existing `conv-context` package — the README's own usage example imports `conv-context`, not `conv-context-next` — consistent with a lookalike lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
